problems: The blind guess (a fish, bird, or sickle/boot-like closed contour) does not identify an ice hook. The silhouette reads as a closed loop or sickle, not as a tool with a grip, a long shaft, and a hooked head.
The blue silhouette is essentially a thin halo around the gold polyline, so it is a copy of the gold lines rather than an independent figure. The outline has no real body mass.
The barb is not readable. The star at (370,317) sits on a small inner lobe and does not visibly curl back up toward the shaft.
The belly star (8102, at about 291,340) and the shank bend (8645, at about 260,241) form a long straight drop on the left. That reads as a boot or leg rather than a hook head.

The grip star (5364, at about 447,240) is a small knob at the right end. The shaft runs left from it, so the tool is oriented horizontally with the hook dropping down on the left. The figure is arguably upright, but the grip and head are not clearly separated.
Labels collide: 'the middle of the long shaft' overlaps 'the upper bend where the shaft...', and 'the belly of the hook' overlaps the gold line. These are hard to read.
output.advice: Redraw so the figure reads as an ice hook silhouette, not a closed loop. Place the grip star 5364 as a clear rounded knob at one end of a straight-ish shaft. Run the shaft through 5799 (upper bend) and 6537 (middle), then have the shaft turn through 8645 (shank bend) and descend into a pronounced hook head. Put 8102 at the deepest point of the hook's belly. Bring 6670 out from the belly so its tip visibly curls back up toward the shaft, creating a real barb. Build a filled or wider silhouette around this path, with real width at the head and the knob, instead of a thin offset halo of the gold lines. Keep the figure upright with the grip at the top and the hook at the bottom. Move the labels off the figure and space them so they do not overlap.
